findings.message: The golden files were not regenerated: only one .claude golden (java-quarkus x-dev-lifecycle) was patched. The byte-for-byte GoldenFileTest will therefore fail for all 17 profiles, and the stories' 'Smoke test: golden file match' DoD is not met. CodexSkillsAssembler copies the generated .claude/skills tree verbatim into .agents/skills and .codex/skills. The .agents golden x-dev-lifecycle/SKILL.md still goes straight from '**Default Behavior:**' (line 133) to '## Phase 0.5 — API-First Contract Generation' (line 137) with no 'Planning Mode Detection'. A grep for 'DoR Pre-check', 'Task-Aware TDD Loop' and '0.2 Resolve Epic Directory' matches only the source SKILL.md files and none of the 17 profiles' .agents goldens (x-dev-implement, x-dev-epic-implement, x-story-plan). GoldenFileTest.profile_whenCalled_matchesGoldenFiles asserts exact equality for each profile.

No automated test was added, although stories 0028-0005 and 0028-0006 each require at least one test checking that the new instructions are present in the SKILL.md. diff.patch changes only SKILL.md/README.md/planning-guide.md resources and one golden file. No file under java/src/test/java is touched. Story DoD: 'Pelo menos 1 teste automatizado validando a presença das novas instruções no SKILL.md' and sub-task '[Test] Unitário: SKILL.md contém instruções de DoR pre-check e per-task checkpoint'.

PRE_PLANNED mode can never be reached from x-story-plan output. That leaves task-by-task Phase 2, the Phase 8 per-task status updates and the epic per-task checkpoint without the input they need. PRE_PLANNED requires all 7 artifacts and credits architecture-, tests-, plan-, security- and compliance-story files to 'x-story-plan Phase 2A/2B/2C'. x-story-plan writes only tasks-story, task-plan-TASK-NNN, planning-report and dor-story (its final 'Artifacts:' list, lines 828-833). The changed DoR checks #1/#2/#3/#9 now treat the planning report as primary and the standalone files only as 'fallback evidence'. Compliance is also conditional, so a non-compliance story never has compliance-story-*.md. A freshly planned story therefore always lands in HYBRID.

Nothing in the change records per-task state during execution or passes it to the story subagent. 'Resume retoma da task exata' therefore has nothing in the checkpoint to resume from. Step 1b says the subagent 'receives the task state and skips DONE tasks automatically'. The subagent prompt template in 1.4 (lines 728-765) passes only story file, branch, phase and skipReview, and the SubagentResult schema has no tasks field. No step sets a task to IN_PROGRESS. x-dev-lifecycle sets tasks.TASK-NNN.status = DONE only in Phase 8, after the whole story. With the default worktree dispatch (1.4a), that write lands in the subagent's worktree, not the orchestrator's execution-state.json. x-dev-implement's resume check reads the filesystem and test results, not execution-state.json.

The DoR pre-check is not in the dispatch algorithms the orchestrator actually follows, so in the default parallel path a NOT_READY story is marked IN_PROGRESS and dispatched. Section 1.1b says the check 'integrates into the Core Loop (Section 1.3) at step 6a' and shows a separate pseudo-code copy with step 'a0'. The real Core Loop in 1.3 is unchanged: '6. ... a. updateStoryStatus(epicDir, storyId, { status: "IN_PROGRESS" }) b. Dispatch subagent'. Steps 4/5 dispatch before step 6. The 1.4a Parallel Worktree Dispatch algorithm (line 783) still says 'For each executable story, mark IN_PROGRESS ... Launch ALL stories' with no DoR step.

The DoR verdict lookup covers only the exact READY / NOT_READY values in a '## Final Verdict' section. A DoR file written in x-story-plan's inline format, or one saying 'NOT READY', matches neither branch, so whether the story is dispatched or blocked is undefined. 1.1b: 'File exists: Read the `## Final Verdict` section'. x-story-plan's inline DoR format (SKILL.md lines 777-815) has no '## Final Verdict' heading; the verdict is in the Header table and '## Summary'. Only _TEMPLATE-DOR-CHECKLIST.md has '## Final Verdict'. story-0028-0001 defines the value as 'READY / NOT READY' (with a space). There is no else-branch for a missing, unparseable or other verdict.

The mode table has no row for 'all 7 artifacts exist but some are stale', and HYBRID reuses only fresh artifacts without saying to regenerate stale ones. A story edited after planning gets an undefined mode. PRE_PLANNED: 'All 7 types exist AND mtime(story) <= mtime(artifact) for all'. HYBRID: 'Some artifacts exist but not all ... Reuse existing fresh ones'. INLINE: 'No artifacts exist'. All present with any stale artifact satisfies none of the three.

The per-task Phase 8 update runs after the lifecycle has already switched to develop. The story-file Section 8.1 edits are therefore made on develop after the PR, never committed to the story branch. The new '### Phase 8 — Per-Task Status Update' is inserted after Phase 8 step '10. `git checkout develop && git pull origin develop`'. It then says 'Update Section 8.1 of the story file: mark each TASK-NNN as Concluida', with no commit or branch instruction.

The task resume check can wrongly mark a task DONE, and can wrongly redo one. A task that modifies an existing class whose current tests pass is skipped. A RED task, whose expected end state is a failing test, is never detected as done. 'Check if the file/class from Implementation Guide exists - If exists, run tests for that component - If tests pass: log "TASK-NNN: DONE (resume point verified)" and skip'. The check does not consult the task's DoD, its commit, or execution-state.json tasks.TASK-NNN.status. x-story-plan task plans carry TDD Phase RED/GREEN/REFACTOR/VERIFY.

Step 1b's BLOCKED-task rule needs task dependencies, but the per-task checkpoint schema has no dependency field and Step 1b doesn't say where to read them. Step 1b: 'BLOCKED tasks: if all task dependencies are DONE -> PENDING'. The Per-Task Fields table in 1.1c lists only status, agent, type, commitSha and duration. Dependencies exist only in tasks-story-*.md / task-plan files, and Step 1b does not reference those files.

The new EPIC_DIR suffix support is only half applied. With a suffixed epic directory, the story-file check aborts, and artifacts are written to and read from the unsuffixed path. Step 0.2 resolves EPIC_DIR to e.g. plans/epic-0028-foo. Step 0.5 still runs 'test -f plans/epic-XXXX/story-XXXX-YYYY.md' and aborts on NOT_FOUND. Step 1.4 (lines 173-176) and outputs 4.2/4.3/4.4 (lines 592, 640, 702) still hard-code 'plans/epic-XXXX/plans/...'. Step 0.2 also leaves undefined the case of several suffix matches with no exact match.

The TPP levels in the QA prompt were reordered (Level 4 = collection, Level 5 = conditional). They now contradict x-test-plan, which DoR check #2 relies on for 'TPP level ordering (1 through 6)', so the two skills will number UT-N levels differently. x-test-plan/SKILL.md lines 131-137: 'TPP Level 4 — Complex Conditions' and 'TPP Level 5 — Iterations'. The diff changes x-story-plan from '4 (conditional) / 5 (collection)', which matched x-test-plan, to '4 (collection) / 5 (conditional)'. No story in epic-0028 asks for this change.

The diff makes several x-story-plan changes that neither story 0028-0005 nor 0028-0006 asks for, which widens what needs review. Changes with no requesting story: EPIC_DIR glob resolution, implementation-map-XXXX.md naming, the new 'implementation' task type in SKILL.md and planning-guide.md, retained SEC tasks as tdd_phase VERIFY, DoR checks #1/#2/#3/#9 now reading planning-report sections, the TPP swap, removal of '(RULE-012)' from the template warning, and a README prerequisite change. The stories only scope x-dev-implement Step 0/2 and x-dev-epic-implement DoR/resume.

The story spec contradicts itself on missing DoR files, and the change picked one reading without recording it. story-0028-0006 §3 and §3.1 say 'Stories sem DoR são BLOCKED' / 'Se NOT_READY ou inexistente: marcar story como BLOCKED'. Its Gherkin and diagram say to proceed when the file is missing. 1.1b implements 'File does NOT exist: Proceed without DoR check'. No note records the choice.

The new '### Phase 0.5 — Planning Mode Detection' shares a phase number with the existing '## Phase 0.5 — API-First Contract Generation', sits under Phase 0's heading level, and is missing from the Workflow Overview. This makes the phase sequence ambiguous. Line 136 '### Phase 0.5 — Planning Mode Detection' is followed by line 165 '## Phase 0.5 — API-First Contract Generation'. The Workflow Overview (lines 35-46) lists only the API-First Phase 0.5.

The docs disagree on who produces the per-task plans and on the commit convention, which can send users to the wrong skill. Line 89 says per-task plans are 'produced by `x-dev-lifecycle`'. The Integration table names `x-lib-task-decomposer`. The plans are actually written by x-story-plan Phase 4.2. The task-aware commit at line 280 is always '[TDD:GREEN]', while x-dev-lifecycle's PRE_PLANNED commit is '[TDD:RED|GREEN|REFACTOR]'.

Task-by-task mode tells an agent that holds commit and shell rights to run whatever the Implementation Guide text in a repository plan file says. Text planted in a story or plan file may therefore be acted on as instructions. 'b. Execute the Implementation Guide instructions' (x-dev-lifecycle) and '##### 3. Execute Implementation Guide — Follow the step-by-step instructions in the task plan' (x-dev-implement). The task plans are model-written from story content (x-story-plan 4.2 '{step-by-step implementation instructions from the proposing agent}'). Neither skill says to treat that text as data or to limit which commands it may trigger.
